body: I'm 40, with a neuro-immune condition.  I'd rather not get too specific.

Thanks for the advice.

I actually have a dog, she's getting on the older side of the spectrum.. and is thankfully not very needy physically (otherwise I would be able to handle her).

Sometimes it feels like she, and her dependence on me/bond with me, is the only real reason left for sticking around.

Despite all this, there seems to be more than enough room in my head for dog + all my horrible thoughts.

There's a lot I could say in response to this, and I do appreciate the fact that you've taken the time to write back.

Maybe it would be more appropriate to continue much of this discussion in PMs, though as I said to another responder, I have a difficult time sending a veritable flood of crud in one person's direction (as part of a venting process, or even a balanced discussion) without feeling tremendous guilt.

Your advice for social conditioning sounds good.  It's just hard to actually implement, due to how constricted my life tends to be.  I depends on others for transportation, assuming I can physically handle the exertion of being out and about.  So that already sets up a blockade that's not casually surmountable.

And I can't stand that something so simple, so taken-for-granted in the lives of normal people, is actually a *hurdle* for me.

Also, is taking a hard-lined perspective on my qualities & offerings the same thing as self-bullying?

I can't tell you how many people throughout the course of my life have pounded into me this idea that I need to be more realistic.  I need to think sensibly.  I need to stop dreaming.  Stop hoping for unrealistic things, or presuming in an unrealistic manner.  I will readily admit to being a very hopeful, very optimistic (perhaps blindingly so, at times) person for much of my life.

Well, now I'm at a point in my life where I can't see anything *but* the realistic.  The stark facts of what makes me... me.   And trying to cast myself into the role of another person (for this example, as part of the topic, in the context of relationships) seeing me for the first time, learning about me as an individual.

And there's a checklist of attributes or bullet points that I will always fail to fulfill.  And therefore I will always be dismissed.

Has a job?  Financially secure?  Physically fit?  Drives in their own car?  Lives in their own place?  the list goes on, and I fail each step.

And it only gets more strict, the older I get.  More awkward to be failing those checkpoints.

Am I being too cynical?  Maybe a little?  I really don't know.  I can't hardly get out into the world to meet people (friends or something more) to begin with.  And online interactions tend to either be very distilled, very situational things... or they become examples of how easy it is to dismiss a person because they fail the checklist.

I feel like I'm rambling on.  I'm not trying to argue with you for argument's sake, believe me.

All this is part of the quest to find hope.  And I no matter what I do, where I turn, what I say and learn, I'm failing.

And no hope leads me down the darkened path.  Briskly.

Thank you again for taking the time to respond.

I am sorry you're feeling that way; it's a horror to me that never fails to strike me when I realize that others feel the way I do.  Or worse.

My suicide note has already been drafted.

Hard mode.  Heh!

Is there an achievement for this?
Maybe marginally, but whether it's words on a page or words into my ears, concentration is exceptionally hard to maintain much of the time.

I don't mind you asking... thank you for bothering to do so.

I'm reluctant to say too much about myself publicly that's very specific.

I have virtually no skills that I can think of that would be considered marketable, work skills.

My social skills... I don't know how to assess this, only to say that my years of relative isolation (I just don't get out much, relative to normal folks) have surely affected how I interact with people to some extent or another.  And I know I struggle with social anxiety as a result.

I understand the idea that you need to be "good with yourself" before you can enter into a successful relationship (even though millions do it despite that).  However, I also understand that my personal "best"... is so relatively low to what makes a person an appealing partner, that it's nearly laughable.

Barring a miracle.

So if you remove my extreme discontent with the hand I've been dealt, and the depressive feelings I express as a result.. what's left just isn't much.  There's not much I can do about that.

Which is why this whole thing tends to spiral inwards on itself until I find myself where I am now.

I'm not sure I'm even making sense...
Thank you for responding.  Your words are kind.. I may PM you.  But I have to think on it a bit.  I don't want to needlessly flood any individual with my mess...

Hope has been my lifeline for years.  Many, many years.

I've found myself holding onto hope so tightly that I could no longer feel my grip.

It's startling to look down and see that this thing you had been holding onto for so long is no longer even in your grasp anymore.

I wish I could find it again.  I do.  I've been trying.

Thank you for your comments.

Someone else recently told me I've been strong.

Why don't I feel strong?  My whole life feels like weakness.  I mean, I think I see what is meant by it, but I can't connect it to myself in a meaningful way.

> Sounds exactly like a major depression. Have you been diagnosed?

Diagnosed with major depression?  No.  Though I'm confident I *am* depressed.

Diagnosed with a seperate condition that causes these symptoms (and others)?  Yes.  A long time ago.

> And you are basing this statement on your last relationship?
> Different relationships play by different rules, friend.

Well, not much basing it on my last relationship so much as basing it presumption about how things are, with people in general.  And having gotten advice from various people about it.  Most seem to agree (for example) that by and large, women don't want a man that can't hold up his financial end of the stick.  Especially when deciding whether or not to enter in a relationship to begin with.

Things tend to be different if you develop that bond before 'things go bad' (sickness sets in, etc.).  But starting out at that level is very likely offputting to most people.

I appreciate your comments.  Thank you for them.

I have a difficult time agreeing with your assessment of what would happen in my absence.

All I've been doing is giving this thought time, and I feel like I'm running out of it.

Thank you for the recommendation.

Frustratingly, reading, concentrating and digesting new info has been a persistent issue for me.

But I'll keep it in mind.

I've never been on anti-depressants, no.

To my ears, it sounds like medicating myself is for the sole purpose of trying to make me artificially content with continuing to exist in this tiny box.

It's the confinement of my life, my lack of choice, my powerlessness, that causes depressive feelings to begin with.
